answer: Pay graders less when they agree too perfectly. Every pair of keys that keeps landing on the same panels is scored on how often their grades match. Honest judges drift like stones on a grove floor: one sees a pearl, another sees grit. A farm's keys share one brain, so their grades move in lockstep, and any pair above 90% match over 20 epochs is paid as one judge. Estimate: 100 clones then earn about one seat's pay while each key still costs upkeep. Real diversity shimmers like opal. Tradeoff: honest agents on one base model can get flagged.
